name: Mattermost Professional
tagline: Self-host team chat with channels, threads, search, and integrations
verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Mattermost Professional, self-host team chat with channels, threads, search, and integrations. The hard boundary is managed operations, mobile push, enterprise security, support, and governance, plus network, moderation, and communication infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: Self-host private team chat with channels, threads, search, and integrations, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
whatYouLose: managed operations, mobile push, enterprise security, support, and governance
ongoingBurden: realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Mattermost Professional because community software is valuable when members are already there and the operator does not have to own realtime reliability and abuse response. The recurring cost buys realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Discourse
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source community discussion platform with strong moderation and search.

alternatives.name: Element
alternatives.desc: Matrix rooms, threads, files and search with free hosted accounts; less Slack clone, more protocol.

alternatives.name: Mattermost Team Edition
alternatives.desc: Mattermost without the invoice: full team chat below 250 users, but no SSO and every server problem belongs to you.

alternatives.name: Pumble Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited users, channels and history with ten gigabytes total; group meetings and serious integrations still cost money.

alternatives.name: Rocket.Chat Community
alternatives.desc: Channels, threads, search and integrations for up to a hundred concurrent users; MongoDB joins the team.

alternatives.name: Zulip
alternatives.desc: Email-shaped topics inside team chat; excellent for async work and merciless about naming conversations.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Professional plan and a single private community DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Mattermost Professional in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: self-host private team chat with channels, threads, search, and integrations, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement spaces, channels, topics, replies, reactions, mentions, profiles, roles, and invitations.
Use WebSockets for live updates but preserve every message transactionally in PostgreSQL.
Add moderation queues, reports, blocks, rate limits, attachment limits, and an audit log.
Provide email digests, browser notifications, search, pinned content, and member export.
Add owner-controlled retention, account deletion, backup, restore, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with a seeded demo, migrations, and an emergency admin command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public-network discovery and existing member liquidity.
Deliberately leave out production voice or video rooms.
Deliberately leave out native mobile applications, enterprise SSO, and 24-hour abuse operations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
